title: OpenAPI describes the likes endpoint as the server behaves: rate-limit 429s, empty cursor and long q
acceptance: The likes 429 response in apps/api/openapi/openapi.json covers the per-user rate limits (provider-likes 20/min, provider-likes-search 30/min) as well as PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED, so a client can tell a short wait from a provider quota failure.
The cursor parameter states minLength 1 (the server answers an empty ?cursor= with 422), or the server treats an empty cursor as the first page; the spec and the code agree.
The q parameter matches the server: either the server rejects q over 200 characters with 422, or the spec says longer q is truncated to 200.
OpenAPI is regenerated, drift and contract-parity pass, and a later iOS PR refreshes web-contract/ (workspace rule: web first).
nextAction: From the iOS #52 final review (2026-10-31). Files: apps/api/scripts/generate-openapi.ts and apps/api/openapi/openapi.json; a server-side change would touch apps/api/src/routes/providers.ts (owner-gated: provider). Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: Final review of iOS #52 (snapshot of web 0a77110), items 1-3: the likes 429 omits the per-user rate limits; cursor lacks minLength though the server rejects empty; q maxLength 200 while the server truncates.
